If it's not fun, why would it be addicting?

They are two different words for a reason.

Things can be fun and addicting.

Or not fun and addicting.

Or fun and not addicting.

Or neither.

But don't assume that they're intrinsically combined.

Just for a minute, consider all the actions you take as either pursuing pleasure or doing chores (chores being things like: going to work, sleeping, paying pills, keeping your exercise regiment and diet in line, laundry, dishes, things that keep a baseline quality of life).

Addiction, then, generally means finding a "pursuit of pleasure" activity that you prioritize so highly that you're willing to forgo "chores" for it.

For example:

"I play the game Stardew Valley and I'm right at the end of winter; I can't wait to play again so I can plant all my spring crops and try out the new irrigation stuff I got" - This doesn't indicate addiction.

"I play farmville during work hours because my crops will die if I wait until my break to water them" - This indicates addiction; the person is prioritizing the game above their job.

The game in the second example is (intentionally or not) engineered to make its players prioritize the game above "chores". This is unsettling because the degree to which people hold a "chores first" mentality has deep implications on how society runs. So fucking with that in order to make money is short-sighted at best and socially destabilizing at worst.
It's not like addicting and fun can't overlap. But the difference is, when it stops being fun, and you still play, rather than it stops being fun, so you stop.
